title: Encrypt S3 With a Customer KMS Key
scenario: Regulated data must use a customer-managed KMS key, not the default SSE-S3 key. Create the key and wire it into the bucket encryption.
constraints: Reference the KMS key from the encryption configuration.

focus.title: Complete the aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration.

hints.why: S3 is usually the first shared service in an AWS configuration. Bucket settings, versioning, encryption and public-access blocks are common review findings.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use S3 when you need durable object storage for assets, logs, backups or static content, and lock down access from the start.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration" "this"`. Use this code shape: bucket; rule { apply_server_side_encryption_by_default { sse_algorithm; kms_master_key_id } }. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.bucket_name`, `aws_kms_key.this.arn`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
